# reac-repacer / fuzz_uci

reac-repacer's own fuzz target `fuzz_uci` ([source](source/fuzz_uci.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-repacer 0.2.3 (FreeREAC/reac-repacer at 3ac1cf10).

Takes a ring-size bit and then, for each of the five hot parameters, a running value and a configuration reply of up to 255 bytes. It reads each reply as an integer, checks that the value is the same when the byte after the reply is "0" and when it is a space, compares it with the value the harness parses itself, and then checks that holding the five values to their ranges gives the ranges the harness defines itself.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of src/repace_wire.c and src/repace_conf.c, and one of libreac's src/reac.c, the files reac-repacer's own libFuzzer build compiles; built as a static riscv64 program for the standard driver in place of libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- A reply's value depends only on the reply's bytes: the same reply followed by "0" and followed by a space gives the same value ([lines 82-103](source/fuzz_uci.c#L82-L103)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The value is the one the reply grammar gives (blanks, an optional sign, decimal digits, then blanks or a CR, on the first line) when it fits an int, and the running value otherwise ([lines 105-133](source/fuzz_uci.c#L105-L133)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each of the five parameters is held to its range, the adaptive maximum to at least the adaptive minimum, and the margin to the ring size less 64 ([lines 135-173](source/fuzz_uci.c#L135-L173)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch reac-repacer` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_uci.plain` | 44,640 | `a6119aa7f1f281cacb63a767e0b5e6976b8f220542f6109c4fd2cecaf98ae5ac` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_uci.ubsan` | 44,936 | `fa87ac3037db248a9ae80eb487b18990df08b26707cb501947d2831f6ccee58c` |
| asan | `fuzz_uci.asan` | 560,936 | `6ea017c24525e6946fa06dc7e3075459ad2c5146d59af49873bf3c51a46e885d` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_uci.asan-ubsan` | 561,192 | `a1b86e424adde6f65d345459822690a6c21e9e606446b91b4ad25e9f3ef6e7fc` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
